summary.intent: Implement part 1 of named Cargo registry support in Callisto: allow a `[registries.<name>]` entry with `kind = "cargo"` as a valid `publish-to` target, then address review and mutation-testing findings and open the PR.
summary.outcome: Pushed a signed commit and opened PR #575 (trail #460). Named cargo registries now pass `--registry <name>` to `cargo publish` and `cargo info`. All gates were green and `cargo mutants --in-diff` reported 0 missed after a fix. Part 2 (Cargo rehearsals and native install/load matrix in #572) is deferred until #575 merges.

repo: Changes are gated by `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test`, plus `cargo mutants --in-diff` run against a diff of `crates/callisto-model/src` and `crates/callisto-graph/src` versus origin/main.
Commits are GPG-signed (`-S`), and GitHub's verification reason is checked via `gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/commits/<sha>`. They carry no session trailer.
Work is done in a git worktree under `.claude/worktrees/wp-cargo-named-registries`, and the branch is pushed with an explicit refspec `HEAD:refs/heads/worktree-wp-cargo-named-registries`.
PRs are linked to trails with `entire trail link <n>` and `entire trail ci-pr --branch <branch>`.
Reusing an existing error code was preferred over adding a new one: only E330's help text and its row in `docs/errors.md` were touched. Adding codes is treated as a larger decision.

A `crates-io` publish runs plain `cargo publish` with no `--registry`, while observation passes `--registry crates-io`. Cargo's own config can redirect the publish, and Callisto then fails with E157 after the upload. This predates the PR.
Named registries need a `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN` env var in the release job. Docs and the changeset now say so.
Built-in publish target names (`none`, `github-release`, `npm`, etc.) always win over a cargo registry declared with the same name.
Docs touched for this feature: `docs/publishing.md`, `docs/config.md`, REL-PUB-06 and REL-PUB-18.

code.finding: `validated_registry_key` lives here and was reused from the graph config resolver (`crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs`) so malformed registry names fail at load with E330 rather than late with E159.
`PublishTarget` gained a `CargoRegistry` variant, and `config_str()` now returns `&str`. Wire output for `crates-io` is unchanged.
This line needed correcting and now describes the `crates-io` publish/observe `--registry` asymmetry.

workflow: Mutation testing caught gaps that normal tests missed: 3 missed mutants in the new variant's `registry_key` and `config_str`, closed with a unit test.
A fresh reviewer agent (Opus) surfaced real issues, including a wrong claim in earlier docs. Amend the unpushed commit, regenerate the diff and rerun mutants after each fix.
Boundary tests were written first and failed first, driving the real binary to assert `--registry my-reg` appears with no `crates-io`.
Edits were scripted through temp Python scripts run with `python3 -I`, with gate output captured to files and grepped for `GATE` and `^error` lines.
The worktree `target/` was deleted after finishing to reclaim disk.

friction: The first push command was combined with several other checks and then re-run separately, suggesting the push or verification step needed splitting to confirm the remote ref.
The first mutation run missed 3 mutants, forcing a fix, an amend, a gate rerun and another mutation run.
An earlier claim in AGENTS.md (#572), that callisto always publishes with `--registry crates-io`, turned out to be wrong.
open_items: Decision needed from the user: should a cargo registry named like a built-in target (`none`, `github-release`, etc.) be rejected at config load? This requires a new error code.
Part 2 is not started and waits for #575 to merge: Cargo rehearsals and the native install/load matrix in #572.
Fix the incorrect AGENTS.md line from #572 about always publishing with `--registry crates-io` in part 2.
No tests cover `confirm-timeout` or `publish-timeout` on a named registry, and nothing pins the fingerprint value for that target.
Pre-existing behaviour left unchanged: Cargo config can redirect a `crates-io` publish, causing E157 after upload.
